audit_findings.title: The normalized legal charge may leave an unpaid $90 million claim outside the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $86.0 million liability at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.73 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation removes the legal provision from OE but does not deduct the remaining settlement liability in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At September 30, 2025 and 2024, the Company had an estimated liability of $ 90.0 and $ 21.0 , respectively, related to these matters that was included in “Other current liabilities” on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error, not merely a possibility: the latest 10-Q reports an $86.0 million liability and scheduled payments after the bridge date. Deducting $86.0 million would reduce bear value from $28.74 to about $28.02 per share and base value from $33.87 to about $33.14; the 30% margin-of-safety threshold would fall from $23.71 to about $23.20. Those levels remain far above the $10.39 price, so the valuation conclusion does not change.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge with an $86.0 million legal-liability deduction, confirming that no corresponding settlement cash payment was already removed from June 30 cash; do not also restore the legal expense to OE.

audit_findings.title: Pre-Spin-off OE years may mix a minority earnings numerator with consolidated cash-flow add-backs
audit_findings.mechanism: An inconsistent claim basis in 2020-2022 OE changes the historical log-trend slope and therefore the $281.2 million anchor used in every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: Immediately prior to completion of the Spin-off, Post owned 71.5% of the economic interests in BellRing LLC, and Old BellRing (and, indirectly, the holders of the Old BellRing Class A Common Stock) owned 28.5% of the economic interests in BellRing LLC.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that pre-Spin-off public holders had only a 28.5% economic interest while the operating group was consolidated. The supplied record does not show the exact numerator and add-back basis used in each OE year, so the valuation error itself remains unresolved. Because the potentially inconsistent years directly determine the anchor rather than merely adjusting the bridge, a proper recast is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2020-2022 OE year by year on one consistent claim basis, document the net-earnings and cash-flow ownership basis for every component, recast to today's 100% common-equity perimeter, and rerun the log trend and anchor-selection step.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may understate the current interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: Q3 2026 interest expense of $19.9 million annualizes to $79.6 million, $11.2 million above FY2025; approximately $8.4 million after tax
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model, additional recurring interest reduces normalized OE directly; debt principal is not separately deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense, net increased $10.1 million during the year ended September 30, 2025 compared to the prior year primarily due to higher outstanding borrowings under our Revolving Credit Facility (as defined in “Liquidity and Capital Resources” within this section).
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates a higher current interest run rate: $19.9 million for the quarter versus $68.4 million for FY2025. Applying the 25.2% FY2025 tax rate gives an approximately $8.4 million annual OE shortfall. At the base scenario's computed valuation multiple, that is about $118 million or $1.00 per share, reducing base value to roughly $32.87 and the buy-below level to about $23.01. This does not change the conclusion relative to the $10.39 price, although persistence of the run rate still requires confirmation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 embedded interest to annualized June-quarter interest, facility fees and financing-cost amortization; if the $8.4 million after-tax shortfall is persistent, rerun the anchor and scenarios with that normalization.

audit_findings.title: Post-service transition may introduce recurring standalone costs absent from historical OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring replacement costs above historical MSA fees would reduce OE and could also lower sustainable growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: There can be no assurance that all of the functions provided to us by Post under the amended and restated master services agreement will be successfully executed by Post or that we will not have to expend significant efforts or costs materially in excess of those estimated in the master services agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q confirms that the MSA expired in March 2026, all functions were transferred, and no MSA fee was incurred in the June quarter. It does not separately disclose the recurring cost of the replacement finance, technology, treasury, insurance, tax and control functions. The transition is therefore no longer merely prospective, but the record cannot distinguish recurring standalone costs from the disclosed reorganization charges or ordinary expense movements, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a post-transition cost bridge by function, separating recurring payroll and third-party costs from the $5.9 million nine-month reorganization charges and discontinued MSA fees, then rerun OE if recurring replacement costs exceed the historical expense embedded in the anchor.

audit_findings.title: A contingent Post tax claim could rank ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: A triggered indemnification or tax-receivable obligation would reduce the equity bridge or create senior recurring cash payments outside ordinary OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Payments under such tax receivable agreement may be substantial, and in certain cases may be accelerated or significantly exceed the actual benefits we realize in respect of the tax attributes subject to the tax receivable agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing describes a contingent claim arising only if the Spin-off's tax treatment fails or another triggering event occurs. It reports no identified facts undermining the tax opinions and supplies no accrued TRA or indemnification liability that can presently be deducted. The possible claim could be substantial, but it is forward-looking and cannot be quantified from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Monitor tax footnotes, IRS examinations, acquisition or issuance activity and disclosures under the tax matters agreement; quantify and rerun the bridge only upon a disclosed trigger, accrual, probable loss range or enforceable payment schedule.

audit_findings.title: Minimum purchase commitments could become unavoidable cash costs in a weak-volume case
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,362.9 million of filed commitments, including $602.7 million due in fiscal 2026; penalty or excess-inventory exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Take-or-pay payments, above-market purchases or unusable inventory would reduce OE and working-capital cash flow, making the 0% growth bear case less adverse than the contractual downside.
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 30, 2025, we had total purchase commitments of $1,362.9 million (with $602.7 million due in fiscal 2026) which extend through fiscal 2033.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitments are demonstrated, but ordinary purchases are already captured in COGS and cannot be deducted again. The record does not establish a volume shortfall, above-market pricing or the fixed payment due for failing to purchase minimum quantities. The latest filing's inventory increase and inventory-related charges warrant monitoring, but they do not quantify a commitment loss.
audit_findings.action: Map committed volumes, prices and remaining terms to current demand forecasts and inventory, obtain the contractual deficiency-payment formulas, and rerun the bear case only for computed penalties, above-market costs or unavoidable excess inventory not already reflected in OE.
